title: AI for Insurance Carriers: Use Cases Across Underwriting, Claims, and Submissions
summary: How insurance carriers use AI in 2026: 12 use cases across submissions, underwriting, and claims, with real results, governance, and where to start.
body_markdown:
**AI for insurance carriers means using artificial intelligence, mostly large language models (LLMs) and AI agents, to read, check, and route the documents behind submissions, underwriting, and claims, so underwriters and adjusters spend their time on decisions instead of data entry.** The highest-value use cases in 2026 are submission intake and clearance, schedule of values (SOV) and loss run extraction, underwriting summaries, policy checking, audits of delegated authority, first notice of loss (FNOL) intake, and claims triage.


In this guide, we walk you through 12 AI use cases carriers are running in production, grouped by where they sit in the workflow. For each one, you'll see what the AI actually does, who owns it, and what results insurers have reported. If you're more interested in comparing vendors rather than use cases, see our separate guide to the[best AI for insurance carriers](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/best-agentic-ai-platform-insurance-carriers) .


## **Key takeaways**


- **Carriers get the fastest return from document-heavy, high-volume work** : submission intake, clearance, SOVs, loss runs, policy checks, and FNOL.
- **Results are measurable in weeks.** Upland Specialty cut clearance time by roughly 30% to 40% within weeks of going live, and a top-10 global carrier reduced SOV intake from up to five days to under 10 minutes.
- **Speed now decides where agents place business.** 90% of independent agents say they've reduced business with a carrier because of workflow friction, according to Ivans.
- **Most carriers haven't scaled yet.** Only 29% of insurers run front-to-back processes through AI agents or automation, per KPMG.
- **Governance is part of the use case.** The NAIC AI Model Bulletin, adopted in 28 states plus DC and Puerto Rico, expects a written AI program that covers vendor systems too.


## **What is AI for insurance carriers?**


AI for insurance carriers is software that applies machine learning, LLMs, and AI agents to the operational work of a risk-bearing insurer. In practice, it reads unstructured documents such as ACORD forms, broker emails, SOVs, loss runs, policies, and claim files, turns them into structured data, checks that data against guidelines, and passes decision-ready work to a person.


It's narrower than "AI for insurance" as a whole. Brokers use AI to build proposals and market risks; MGAs use it to scale delegated authority. Carriers carry the risk, so their use cases cluster around three things: deciding which risks to write, writing them accurately, and paying claims correctly. For the broader market view, see our guide to the[best AI platforms for insurance](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/ai-platforms-for-insurance-companies) .


## **Why carriers are investing in AI now**


Three pressures are pushing carriers from pilots toward production.


**Underwriters still spend a third of their time on non-core work.** Accenture's latest underwriting survey found commercial P&C underwriters spend 35% of their time on non-core activities, as reported by[Insurance Journal](https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2025/12/24/852124.htm) . That's time spent keying, chasing, and reconciling rather than pricing risk.


**Distribution rewards the easiest carrier to work with.** In the[2026 Ivans survey of more than 700 agents](https://www.ivans.com/blog/posts/what-it-takes-for-carriers-to-win-agents-2026/) , 90% said they'd reduced business with a carrier because of workflow friction, 74% named re-keying as a top pain point, and 79% asked carriers for more commercial submission automation. A simple quoting process now outranks commission as a placement driver by nearly two to one.


**The claims workforce is shrinking.**[The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/claims-adjusters-appraisers-examiners-and-investigators.htm) employment of claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators to decline 6% from 2025 to 2035, while claim volume and documentation keep growing.


Most carriers know this. In[KPMG's September 2026 survey](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2026/09/insurers-see-ai-leadership-gaps-remain.html) of insurance leaders across 20 countries, 68% said moving too slowly on AI is a bigger risk than moving too fast. Yet only 29% run front-to-back processes through AI agents or automation, and just 11% have a very clear view of AI return on investment. The gap between intent and production is where the use cases below come in.

## **How AI speeds up submission intake and clearance for carriers**


Submissions are where most carriers start, because the work is repetitive, the volume is high, and every hour saved shows up in quote turnaround. If you're shortlisting tools for this stage, our guide to[submission processing platforms for carriers](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/insurance-submission-processing-platforms) compares the options.


### 1. Submission intake and triage


AI reads the broker's email and every attachment, identifies each document type, and extracts the fields your underwriting system needs: named insured, class codes, limits, exposures, and loss history. It then ranks the submission by fit so underwriters see the best opportunities first. One of the largest MGAs in the US, writing more than $1.5B in premium, cleared submissions[30x faster](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/submissions-processing-ai) after moving intake to FurtherAI. Our[FurtherAI Accelerator for PolicyCenter](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/furtherai-accelerator-guidewire-policycenter) carries the same flow into Guidewire PolicyCenter with no re-keying.


### 2. Clearance and appetite screening


Clearance checks whether a risk is already in-house, whether it fits appetite, and which underwriter should own it. It's rule-heavy but full of judgment calls, which is why many teams assumed it couldn't be automated.[Upland Specialty](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/upland-specialty-proved-furtherai-in-production-then-cut-clearance-time) runs every submission for about a dozen lines of business through one clearance desk. After handing FurtherAI the same rulebook it uses to train clearance staff, Upland cut clearance time by roughly 30% to 40%, with benefits showing up within weeks. At the $1.5B MGA mentioned above, that 30x came from average clearance time falling from about 32 minutes to about one. New to the topic? Start with[what submission clearance is](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/what-is-submission-clearance) .


### 3. SOV extraction and enrichment


Large property schedules can run from 500 to 100,000 locations with up to 60 fields each. A top-10 global carrier with more than $20B in gross written premium used to spend one to five days processing each SOV, and quote turnaround stretched to two to three weeks. With FurtherAI extracting, validating, and enriching 32 critical property fields, intake now takes[under 10 minutes even for 50,000-location SOVs](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/complex-property-sov-intake) , at more than 95% field-level accuracy at go-live (rising to 97% within six months) and a 646% ROI.


### 4. Loss run analysis


Loss runs arrive in dozens of carrier formats, and underwriters often re-key them before they can judge frequency and severity. AI ingests PDFs, spreadsheets, and CSVs, normalizes the fields, and produces a summary of paid, reserved, and open claims. FurtherAI's[loss run automation](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/loss-runs) cuts manual effort by about 70% and compresses the cycle from weeks to same day. For the fundamentals, see[how to read a loss run report](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/how-to-read-a-loss-run-report) .


## **How insurance carriers use AI in underwriting**


Once data is clean, AI can help underwriters reason over it. For complex commercial risks, the aim is a complete, checked file in front of every underwriter, with more time left for the calls only they can make. Our full guide to[AI for underwriting](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/ai-for-underwriting) covers this stage in depth, and[our 2026 underwriting ROI benchmarks](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/how-ai-improves-underwriting) show what to expect.


### 5. Underwriting summaries and guideline checks


AI drafts a summary of the risk, compares it with your underwriting guidelines, and flags breaches, missing information, and out-of-appetite exposures, each linked to the source page. The underwriter reviews, edits, and decides. At Euclid Program Managers, a platform for specialty MGAs, co-founder Nick Colis told us an underwriter who handled[$10M of premium without AI can now handle $15M](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/euclid-program-managers-underwriter-capacity-furtherai) , a 50% lift in capacity.


### 6. Policy checking and comparison


Checking that a quote, binder, and issued policy match, or comparing a renewal with last year's wording, is slow and error-prone by hand. A mid-sized insurer with more than 1,500 employees used FurtherAI to run[policy checks 20x faster](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/policy-check-compare-ai-teammate) and saw a 400% ROI within months. The same capability supports excess underwriting by quickly extracting primary policy terms.


### 7. Audits of delegated underwriting authority


Carriers that write through MGAs must prove those MGAs stay within binding authority. Manual audits review only a sample of files and still take hundreds of hours. A reinsurer supporting more than 100 MGAs spent about 200 hours per MGA audit, half of it on data extraction. FurtherAI automated about five hours of work per file and[cut audit time 45%, to roughly 110 hours](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/underwriting-audit-ai) . Our guide to[underwriting audit automation for carriers](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/underwriting-audit-automation-carriers) covers this use case in detail.


### 8. Risk control and risk engineering


Risk control engineers spend hours on the process work around each engagement, from organizing documents to writing up recommendations. AI moves that work through in the background and pulls the expert in only where their judgment is needed.[GForce Innovations, Grange Insurance's innovation arm](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/grange-gforce-innovations-furtherai-risk-control) , selected FurtherAI for exactly this work in commercial lines risk control.


## **How AI helps carriers with claims processing**


Claims is the second big area of carrier AI, and it's where cycle time is most visible to policyholders. In J.D. Power's[2026 U.S. Property Claims Satisfaction Study](https://jdpower.com/business/press-releases/2026-us-property-claims-satisfaction-study) , claims were fully resolved 3.4 days faster than a year earlier, and faster cycle times helped lift satisfaction despite higher premiums. For a vendor comparison at this stage, see our list of[AI tools for claims processing](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/best-ai-tools-insurance-claims-processing) .


### 9. FNOL and claims intake


Intake is high-volume, repetitive, and full of inconsistent layouts. A specialty insurer handling more than 3,000 claims a year spent about 2.5 hours of staff time on each new claim, roughly 7,500 hours annually. After deploying FurtherAI, it automated more than 90% of the intake process, processed claims more than 10x faster, and saved more than $360K at a[568% ROI](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/claims-processing-ai) .


### 10. Triage and assignment


AI scores each new claim for complexity, severity, and litigation risk, then routes it to the right adjuster or a fast-track queue. McKinsey reports that Aviva, using more than 80 AI models in claims, improved[routing accuracy by 30% and cut liability assessment time on complex cases by 23 days](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/tech-and-ai/how-we-help-clients/rewired-in-action/aviva-rewiring-the-insurance-claims-journey-with-ai) . See how commercial teams approach[claims triage and adjuster assignment](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/commercial-claims-triage-adjuster-assignment) .


### 11. Claim document review


Adjusters lose much of their day pulling documents and cross-referencing systems before the real claims work starts. AI summarizes medical records, bills, estimates, photos, and correspondence into a single view with citations back to each page.[RMA Insurance](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/rma-insurance-partners-with-furtherai) , a Canadian reinsurance and insurance services company, chose FurtherAI as the foundation for modernizing its claims operations for this reason.


### 12. Leakage, fraud, and post-payment audits


Traditional claims audits review a small sample. AI can test every open and closed file against coverage terms, reserve rules, and payment controls, so overpayments and missed recoveries surface before they compound.[Deloitte estimates](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/financial-services-industry-outlooks/insurance-industry-outlook/2026.html) that AI-driven, real-time fraud analytics could save P&C insurers up to $160B by 2032. Our guide to[claims leakage and fraud detection software](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/claims-leakage-fraud-detection-software-for-carriers) compares the tools.


## **Where should an insurance carrier start with AI?**


Start with one workflow that scores well on four questions:


1. **Is it high-volume?** A task you run thousands of times a year pays back faster than one you run weekly.
2. **Is it document-heavy?** AI earns its keep turning unstructured documents into structured data.
3. **Can you measure it today?** Minutes per submission, hours per audit, and days to close give you a clean baseline.
4. **Does a person still make the final call?** Keeping humans on the decision lowers regulatory and reputational risk while trust builds.


For most carriers, that points to submission intake, clearance, or FNOL. Then prove accuracy before you switch it on. Upland ran FurtherAI in shadow mode, writing extractions to a hidden field while staff kept working by hand, and turned it on once agreement cleared 85%. Our guide on[how to deploy AI in production](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/how-to-deploy-ai-in-production-for-insurance) walks through that approach.


Data readiness matters as much as the model. Arron Lamp, who runs technology for Tokio Marine HCC's Public Risk Group, told us his team spent a little over a year getting data and services into shape[before scaling AI](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/deploying-ai-scale-tokio-marine-hcc-playbook) . Once one workflow works, the extracted data feeds the next: clean submission data improves underwriting summaries, which improve audits. To see how these pieces connect, read about the[AI agents for insurance](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/ai-agents-for-insurance) that hand work to each other on a single file.


## **What regulations apply to carriers using AI?**


In the US, the main framework is the NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems by Insurers, adopted in December 2023. As of November 13, 2026,[28 states plus the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico](https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/legal-adoption-map-ai-model-bulletin.pdf) have adopted it, and California, Colorado, and New York have their own insurance-specific AI rules.


The bulletin expects each insurer to maintain a written AI systems program with governance, risk management, and internal controls, and it applies to AI systems bought from third parties as well as those built in-house. For a carrier, that turns into practical requirements for every use case above:


- A traceable link from every AI output to its source document
- Human review on decisions that affect coverage, pricing, or claim payment
- A log of every action the system takes, available for market conduct exams
- Accuracy testing before go-live and ongoing monitoring for drift


Our[complete guide to AI governance in insurance](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/ai-governance-insurance-complete-guide) covers how to build that program.


## **How do carriers measure ROI from AI?**


Measure one workflow at a time. Capture a baseline before launch, then track:


- **Cycle time:** minutes to clear a submission, days to quote, days to close a claim
- **Touch time:** staff hours per file
- **Accuracy:** field-level accuracy against a reviewed sample
- **Capacity:** premium or claims handled per person
- **Growth signals:** quote and bind ratios, broker submission volume


Few insurers do this well. Only 11% of insurance leaders say they have a very clear view of AI ROI, according to[KPMG](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2026/09/insurers-see-ai-leadership-gaps-remain.html) . Carriers that measure tend to find the gains compound: faster responses bring in more submissions from the brokers they already work with. For cost benchmarks and pricing models, see our breakdown of[AI for insurance operations costs and ROI](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/the-real-roi-of-ai-in-commercial-insurance-operations) .

## **Frequently asked questions**


#### What are the most common AI use cases for insurance carriers?


The most common AI use cases for insurance carriers are submission intake and triage, clearance, SOV and loss run extraction, underwriting summaries, policy checking, delegated authority audits, FNOL intake, claims triage, and claim document review. They share three traits: high volume, heavy reliance on unstructured documents, and a measurable baseline. That makes results easy to measure against a clear before-and-after baseline.


#### How are insurance carriers using AI in underwriting?


Carriers use AI to prepare decision-ready files while underwriters keep the judgment calls. AI extracts data from applications, SOVs, and loss runs, drafts a risk summary, checks it against underwriting guidelines, and flags gaps or breaches with links to the source. Underwriters then review and decide. Results include a 50% lift in premium handled per underwriter at Euclid and SOV intake cut from days to minutes at a top-10 carrier.


#### How does AI help carriers with claims processing?


AI speeds up the parts of claims that slow adjusters down. It reads FNOL notices and attachments, opens the claim, routes it by complexity, summarizes medical records and estimates, and audits files for leakage. One specialty insurer automated more than 90% of claims intake with FurtherAI, processed claims more than 10x faster, and saved more than $360K, a 568% ROI.


#### Where should an insurance carrier start with AI?


Start with one high-volume, document-heavy workflow that you can measure today and where a person still makes the final decision. Submission intake, clearance, and FNOL intake usually fit best. Run the AI in shadow mode against your team's work, set an accuracy threshold before go-live, and expand only once results hold. Upland Specialty switched on after agreement cleared 85%.


#### Will AI replace underwriters and claims adjusters?


No. In carrier deployments today, AI takes over data entry, document review, and first-pass checks, while underwriters and adjusters keep the decisions on coverage, pricing, and payment. Nearly half of insurers' AI budgets go to operational and back-office efficiency, according to KPMG. Regulators also expect human oversight: the NAIC Model Bulletin asks insurers to govern AI decisions that affect consumers, including systems bought from vendors.


#### What regulations apply to insurance carriers using AI?


In the US, the NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of AI Systems by Insurers is the main framework, adopted in 28 states plus DC and Puerto Rico as of November 2026. It requires a written AI program with governance, risk controls, and vendor oversight. California, Colorado, and New York have separate insurance-specific AI rules, so check each state where you write business.


#### How do carriers measure ROI from AI?


Carriers measure ROI by comparing one workflow before and after launch. Track cycle time, staff hours per file, field-level accuracy, and capacity per person, then weigh the gains against license, implementation, and maintenance costs. Published FurtherAI carrier results include a 646% ROI on SOV intake and a 568% ROI on claims intake. Only 11% of insurers report a very clear view of AI ROI.
